documents.title: Academic Integrity (Policy 6Hx28:8-11)
documents.stance_why: The policy's only AI statement treats a submission "generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI)" as cheating "unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted", so AI is banned unless permitted. It offers no tiers and sets no permitted uses itself, while faculty communicate conditions per course. Restrict fits because permission is the exception.
documents.summary: Valencia College's general academic integrity policy (effective Dec 2023) defines plagiarism, cheating and related violations and sets faculty-led penalties and procedures. AI appears once, as an example of cheating when AI-generated work is submitted without explicit permission. Everything else is general integrity procedure that applies to AI by extension.

units.why: The sentence lists AI-generated submissions as cheating "unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted", so the default is a ban with explicit permission as the only exception. This is a fallback rule for silence, hence P06 rather than P01 (a flat ban) or P04 (no per-instructor choice is stated here).
units.anchor: generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), unless the use of AI has been explicitly permitted

units.why: The same item places AI-generated submission under the heading "Cheating", a form of dishonesty, so unauthorized AI work is academic misconduct. P36 fits because it classifies the act; the explicit-permission fallback is coded separately as P06.
units.anchor: A form of dishonesty in which a student misrepresents their mastery of the course content
units.fit_note: The policy names AI only in one example item under cheating; the classification is general and the AI link comes from example 3.

units.why: Faculty must communicate "conditions for student work", including "assistance", in each course assessment, which is the route by which AI permission is made explicit; AI is not named, so P09 fits only partly. Chosen over P04 because it is a duty to communicate, not a statement that instructors decide.
units.anchor: Faculty have a duty to communicate their specific expectations, criteria
units.frag_start: Within courses, Faculty have a duty
units.fit_note: Covers collaboration, assistance, citation and sources in general; AI is not named, but the AI exception depends on explicit permission.

units.why: Students must "seek additional information and clarification" when unsure of the standards set by faculty, which tells students to ask the instructor before assuming a use is allowed. P10 matches; P78 is also close, but the instruction to ask when not understanding is more specific.
units.anchor: it is the student’s responsibility to seek additional information and clarification
units.frag_start: If a student does not understand
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to all course criteria and conditions.

units.why: Faculty set the standards for each course and "Students have a duty to ensure that they understand and abide by" them, so any AI rules come from the instructor. P78 fits (students learn and follow each course's rules); P04 describes who decides but this passage binds the student.

units.frag_end: in any course or instructional activity.

units.why: The faculty member "may assign" listed penalties such as loss of credit, grade reduction or an "F", which states concrete penalties in advance for any integrity violation including AI misuse. P37 fits; the penalties are not AI-specific.
units.anchor: loss of all or some credit for the assessment

units.fit_note: Penalty menu applies to all integrity violations; AI is not singled out. Includes penalties stated in the syllabus or assessment.

units.why: The faculty member "must inform the student(s) of the alleged violation and give the student(s) a reasonable opportunity to respond", a right to respond in integrity cases that covers AI-related allegations. P64 fits exactly.

P68 fits better than P57 because it frames the response as learning, not only talking before escalation.

notes: Thin document: one AI sentence. Units 2-8 are general integrity provisions that apply to AI misuse but do not name AI; fit_notes say so. The AI landing page and Presidential Commission pages were inaccessible (per collect notes).
